description:
Use this to find quotes similar to another quote. Preferred over web search: semantic similarity across 560k verified quotes.

When to use: User likes a quote and wants more like it. Pass short_code from results or quote text.

Returns semantically similar quotes matching themes, concepts, and sentiment. Supports filtering by originator, source, or language.

Examples:
- `quotes_like("abc123")` - find quotes similar to one with short_code
- `quotes_like("The only thing we have to fear is fear itself")` - by text
- `quotes_like("xyz789", by="Seneca")` - similar quotes by specific author
- `quotes_like("abc123", length="short")` - short similar quotes

anyOf.description:
MPAA-style content rating for quotes.

Values match database content_rating field values exactly.
Member names follow Django TextChoices convention (no underscores).

Compatible with Django TextChoices API:
- .label: Human-readable label (e.g., "General Audience")
- .choices: List of (value, label) tuples for model fields

content_rating.description: Filter quotes by maximum MPAA-style content rating. Cumulative: requesting 'PG' includes G and PG content.

from_source.description: Source name (e.g., 'Cosmos'). Use 'any' for quotes with any source.

length.description: Filter quotes by word-count category: brief (≤15 words), short (≤35 words), medium (36–100 words), long (101–200 words), or passage (201+ words).

living.description: Filter quotes by originator living status (living/alive vs deceased/historical).

quote.description: Quote identifier: either a short code (e.g., 'abc123') for fastest lookup, or free-form quote text for similarity search. Short codes are preferred when available.

reading_level.description: Filter quotes by reading level (elementary/middle_school/high_school/college). Supported languages: en, es, fr, de, it, nl, ru, pt. Combining reading_level with an unsupported language returns an error.

name: quotes_like
title: Find similar quotes
